topic: Incoming missile identity survives launcher crew loss
findings: CortexAAObserve captures vehicle _shooter but no launch-time affiliation or native projectile-parent receipt.
CortexAAAllocate filters retained tracks, NOTICE admission and dispatch against current side of original launcher.
CortexAAIntercept START and STEP repeat current-launcher hostility checks; STEP retires THREAT_ENDED on source deletion.
CortexAAInterceptEffect additionally requires non-null original source and current hostility, and compares native incoming projectile parent with that source.
requiredResolution: Capture immutable launch affiliation only from authenticated native warning and matching actual projectile parents.
Carry exact projectile identity and original owner epoch and finite lifetime through allocation and execution; duplicate warning must not refresh expiry.
Distinguish launcher deletion or crew loss from missile destruction, retargeting and defended-asset loss.
Keep current owner, ROE, mission/task supersession and friendly/civilian collateral vetoes.
Do not treat two null objects as proof of matching launch provenance; retain conservative scripted-fuse refusal where original parent evidence is unavailable.
Extend existing AA observation regression cases; full build and independent candidate verification after coherent implementation.
limitations: No Arma audit launched; audits remain paused.
This source review identifies premature retirement paths; it does not prove the engine event or deletion behaviour in a live mission.

Launch affiliation means affiliation authenticated at the first native warning, not historical reconstruction of the original firing event. A source already unidentifiable or friendly at that first warning cannot establish a hostile receipt.

implementation.receipt: One machine-private exact projectile/launcher/parent/affiliation record with immutable original15s expiry.
consumers: CortexAAInterceptEffect retained non-null launcher and native-parent veto
implementation.cost: No scan/timer/worker; fixed two-parent comparison at existing validation points.
